Photograph: Oleksandr Gimanov/AFP/Getty Images Russia-Ukraine war at a glance Ukraine Explainer Ukraine war briefing: Nine killed and dozens wounded in Russian strikes as Kyiv braces for harsh winter Zelenskyy says ‘Russia wants to kill the Ukrainian economy’ as Moscow steps up attacks on infrastructure. What we know on day 1,663

Prefer the Guardian on Google Russian airstrikes killed nine people, injured dozens and damaged buildings and infrastructure across Ukraine on Saturday, as Kyiv braces for a “very difficult” winter amid intensified attacks on the country. The civilian death toll has risen sharply in Ukraine over the past two ⁠months as Russia steps up attacks ⁠on power plants and other ​infrastructure. Ukraine has hit energy facilities and warehouses in distant parts of Russia, and both sides have targeted each other’s shipping.

Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy, writing on Telegram, said Russia had deployed nearly 500 drones against Ukrainian targets since ⁠early morning. “Basically, the Russians have expanded the war away from the front, where they have no success, into the economy, and their tactics are as basic as it gets: destroying every site that could help people cope with the conditions of war,” he wrote. “Russia ⁠wants to kill the Ukrainian economy and break our resistance.”

The city council in Kramatorsk , one of Ukraine’s frontline “fortress cities” that Russia wants to capture, ​ said Russian forces attacked private cars, killing three people in three incidents over ‌a 90-minute period . Four people were injured. “These ‌are not military targets,” the council said. “They are ordinary civilian cars. People were going about their business.”

article.title: Russian attacks on Kyiv petrol stations kill two, Ukrainian strikes kill three in Russia
article.description: Sept 11 (Reuters) - Russia attacked two Kyiv petrol stations with jet-powered drones early on Friday, killing two people in an escalation of strikes that President Volody… Leggi
paragraphs: Sept 11 (Reuters) - Russia attacked two Kyiv petrol stations with jet-powered drones early on Friday, killing two people in an escalation of strikes that President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said were becoming “increasingly terrorist in nature.”
Three more people were killed in Russian strikes in southeastern Ukraine’s Dnipropetrovsk and Zaporizhzhia regions and in Kharkiv in the northeast, according to the governors of those regions.
Ukraine also carried out drone attacks on Russia, killing two people in the Tula region overnight and one on Friday in the Kursk region, local officials said.

With fighting on the front line largely stalled more than 4-1/2 years into the war in Ukraine, Russia and Ukraine increasingly have struck logistics and other economic targets in recent weeks to try to damage the other’s war effort.

Russia has for two weeks been carrying out almost constant attacks with faster jet-powered drones that have killed a number of Kyiv residents and disrupted daily life in Ukraine’s capital. The attacks were paused while U.S. peace negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner visited Kyiv at the weekend, but then resumed.

By Sophie Tanno, Daria Tarasova-Markina, and Lex Harvey, CNN

(CNN) — US President Donald Trump urged his Ukrainian counterpart, Volodymyr Zelensky, to stop targeting Russia’s diesel fuel in aerial attacks, claiming that it is “hurting the world,” as the war in Iran continues to spike global oil prices.

Ukraine has been pummeling Russian fuel infrastructure for months, severely reducing Moscow’s refining capacity and triggering widespread supply shortages. In response, Russia, the world’s second largest diesel exporter behind the US, has banned the foreign sale of its diesel.
“Mr. Zelensky has to do one thing. He has to stop knocking out diesel fuel in Russia…because he’s causing a shortage of diesel,” Trump said during an official visit to Ireland on Sunday.

article.title: Russian drone strikes near Polish border hit truck and train, Kyiv says attacks target NATO
article.description: A Russian drone struck near the Yahodyn border crossing, and another hit a passenger train locomotive in Ukraine
paragraphs: Top stories Israel Middle East Israel elections 2026 International INNOV'NATION Videos Radio Shows Schedules Channels Profiles en English Français عربى עברית Live i24NEWS International Ukraine-Russia War Russian drone strikes near Polish border hit truck and train, Kyiv says attacks target NATO's doorstep Russian drone strikes near Polish border hit truck and train, Kyiv says attacks target NATO's doorstep A Russian drone struck near the Yahodyn border crossing, and another hit a passenger train locomotive in Ukraine's Volyn region, both within a few kilometers of Poland

i24NEWS 3 min read 3 min read ■ Russia Poland Ukraine Drone attack Google News Follow us Follow Firefighters put out a fire at warehouse stores after a Russian air attack in Odesa, Ukraine, Sunday, Sept. 13, 2026 (AP Photo/Michael Shtekel) A Russian drone struck a truck less than a kilometer (half a mile) from the Polish border near the Dorohusk-Yahodyn crossing, destroying the vehicle, Border Guard spokesman Maj. Dariusz Sienicki told Polish news outlet Wirtualna Polska. The crossing itself was not hit, and traffic between the two countries is flowing normally.
No one was injured on the Polish side, according to Interior Ministry spokeswoman Karolina Gałecka.

Separately, Ukrainian state railway operator Ukrzaliznytsia said a drone struck the locomotive of a passenger train in the Volyn region, two kilometers (about a mile) from the Polish border, with no injuries reported. The company said a monitoring team had warned the train crew of the threat.

Polish Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said Polish systems detected an attack by about a dozen Russian Geran-5 jet-powered drones in western Ukraine, with one striking about a kilometer from the Polish border and another about five kilometers (3.1 miles) away. "Our airspace was protected by F-16s, helicopters and a Saab airborne early warning aircraft. There was no violation of our border," he wrote on X.

article.title: Palestinian Killed, Two Die From Wounds, In Gaza
article.description: A Palestinian was killed in an Israeli drone strike on Monday, while two others, including a child, died from wounds sustained in earlier Israeli attacks. S ...
paragraphs: A Palestinian was killed in an Israeli drone strike on Monday, while two others, including a child, died from wounds sustained in earlier Israeli attacks. Several others were wounded in separate assaults across the Gaza Strip amid ongoing bombardment and reported ceasefire violations.
Medical sources at Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, in southern Gaza, confirmed that one Palestinian was killed and several others were wounded, some seriously, in the drone strike.

They said the incident occurred when an Israeli military drone fired a missile at a motorcycle carrying two Palestinians in the Al-Mawasi area, west of Khan Younis. Several passersby were also wounded in the attack.
Medical and local sources reported that Sobhi Al-Batrikhi succumbed to wounds sustained Sunday night when Israeli forces targeted Palestinians near the Communications Junction, west of Gaza City.
A six-year-old child, Dawood Moqat, also died from wounds sustained weeks earlier when Israeli forces shot him in the Zarqa area of the Tuffah neighborhood, northeast of Gaza City.

article.title: Israeli Attacks Continue Across Gaza as Humanitarian Crisis Deepens
article.description: In the Gaza Strip, Israeli military violations continued amid escalating humanitarian concerns, while Gaza's Health Ministry reported a rising death to ...
paragraphs: In the Gaza Strip, Israeli military violations continued amid escalating humanitarian concerns, while Gaza’s Health Ministry reported a rising death toll and additional casualties despite the ceasefire that took effect on October 10, 2025.

Medical sources reported that a Palestinian woman died on Saturday evening from wounds sustained in an earlier Israeli attack on the Maghazi refugee camp in central Gaza. They identified her as Latifa Ziad Jabr and said she had been critically injured in an Israeli strike on the refugee camp three months earlier. Her husband, Saqer Abu Karim, was previously killed.

Israeli forces opened fire toward displacement tents in the Sudaniya area of northwestern Gaza, moderately wounding a Palestinian child. In a separate incident, an Israeli airstrike on the Tuffah neighborhood, northeast of Gaza City, injured three Palestinians.

Local sources reported that, before dawn, Israeli quadcopter drones dropped explosive devices near homes on Mushtaha Street and by the Shuja’iyya market, east of Gaza City. No injuries were reported. At the same time, heavy gunfire from Israeli military positions east of the city targeted nearby neighborhoods.

In southern Gaza, Israeli artillery shelled areas northwest of Rafah, while Israeli military vehicles opened heavy fire toward southern parts of Khan Younis. Israeli naval vessels also fired toward the coast of Khan Younis.

paragraphs: --> Home World Israeli army ‘kills first, then seeks justification’ for Gaza strikes, says veterans group chief Weiman said Israel seeks to “retrospectively” justify strikes by linking victims to Hamas or Islamic Jihad

REUTERS The Israeli army “kills first, then thinks and tries to find a reason” afterward to justify strikes on the Gaza Strip, said the executive director of Israeli veterans' group Breaking the Silence.

In an interview Friday with France 24 , Nadav Weiman said the army and Israeli authorities seek to “retrospectively” legitimize attacks by attempting to establish links between victims and Hamas or Palestinian Islamic Jihad after strikes have taken place.

“In cases like this Nasser hospital or the 15 paramedics that were killed by IDF (Israeli army) soldiers in Rafah, or air strikes that are killing three-digit numbers of civilians in Gaza ... suddenly the IDF spokesperson in the state of Israel needs to explain to the international community what we did over there and who are the targets for the attack,” Weiman said.

On Aug. 25, 2025, an Israeli attack on the Nasser Medical Complex in the southern Gaza Strip killed at least 20 Palestinians, including patients, health workers, civil defense personnel, and press crews, while several others were injured in the attack, according to the enclave’s Health Ministry.

article.description: Pakistan condemned drone attacks on Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline, calling them a violation of international law and expressing solidarity with the Kingdom
paragraphs: Summary Pakistan condemned drone attacks on Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline, calling them a violation of international law and expressing solidarity with the Kingdom

ISLAMABAD (Dunya News) – Pakistan strongly condemned the reprehensible drone attacks on the East-West Pipeline in Riyadh and Madinah regions of Saudi Arabia, causing damage to the pipeline and injuries to civilians.

These attacks and targeting of civilian infrastructure are a flagrant violation of the international law as well as sovereignty and territorial integrity of the brotherly Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and pose a serious threat to regional peace, security and stability.

Pakistan reaffirmed its unwavering support for the sovereignty, territorial integrity, security and prosperity of the Kingdom, and reiterates its solidarity with the leadership, Government and brotherly people of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
Pakistan has been and will continue to make earnest efforts for achieving lasting peace and stability in the region.

KABUL (Pajhwok): The Iraqi government has confirmed that recent drone attacks on Saudi Arabia’s key East-West oil pipeline were launched from Iraqi territory, prompting Baghdad to dismiss a military commander and launch an investigation.
The Associated Press reported that Iraqi officials had determined that the attacks were launched from Maysan province in southern Iraq, near the Iranian border.

article.description: Pakistan is considering launching airstrikes against the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen at Saudi Arabia’s request, according to Pakistani sources cited by the Turkish outlet Türkiye Today. One of the main objectives would reportedly be to eliminate Houthi forces from Saada province and other areas controlled by the militia. Pakistani Defense Minister Khawaja Asif warned that […]
paragraphs: Pakistan is considering launching airstrikes against the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen at Saudi Arabia’s request, according to Pakistani sources cited by the Turkish outlet Türkiye Today.
One of the main objectives would reportedly be to eliminate Houthi forces from Saada province and other areas controlled by the militia.

Pakistani Defense Minister Khawaja Asif warned that any attack against Saudi Arabia could activate the “Mecca Alliance,” a joint defense agreement signed on August 7 by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.
Under the agreement, an attack against one of the member countries would be considered an attack against all three.

The reported move comes hours after a large-scale Houthi attack in which dozens of drones and ballistic missiles were launched toward the Saudi Air Force base in Khamis Mushait, as well as facilities belonging to the Saudi state-owned oil company in Abha, Najran and Jizan.

paragraphs: JERUSALEM, Sept. 7 (Xinhua) -- An Israeli man was seriously wounded in a stabbing attack near Nablus in the occupied West Bank on Monday, before the suspected attacker was shot dead by Israeli troops, the military and police said.
The attack took place at the unauthorized Ma'oz Yehuda outpost near the Palestinian village of Osarin.

The military said troops imposed a lockdown on villages in the area and launched a search for the suspect. After locating his vehicle, soldiers encountered him and shot him dead when he attempted to stab them, according to the military.
Israeli emergency services said the wounded man, in his 20s, was evacuated by helicopter for medical treatment.

The attack came hours after a 20-year-old Palestinian dentistry student was shot dead in the village of Hajja near Qalqilya during a raid by Israeli settlers, according to the Palestinian Health Ministry. Two other Palestinians were wounded, one seriously.

paragraphs: RAMALLAH/JERUSALEM, Sept. 7 (Xinhua) -- A Palestinian man was shot dead by Israeli forces on Monday after he allegedly stabbed and wounded an Israeli man in the northern West Bank, according to Israeli and Palestinian sources.

Israel's state-owned Kan TV News reported that an Israeli man sustained moderate to serious injuries in what it described as a "terrorist stabbing attack" near the village of Usarin, east of Nablus city.
According to Kan, the Palestinian assailant arrived at the scene in a commercial vehicle, got out, stabbed the Israeli man, and fled.
Later, the Israeli army said in a statement that the troops located the "terrorist" and eliminated him, adding it will "continue to operate to thwart terrorism and maintain security."

Palestinian security sources said Israeli forces tightened military measures around villages south of Nablus, closing military gates at the entrances and preventing residents from entering or leaving.
